newsitem.title: MAURITANIA: Mauritania detains four over Libya links.
newsitem.headline: Mauritania detains four over Libya links.

text.p: Mauritanian security forces have detained four politicians, including the head of the main opposition Action for Change party, on accusations of suspect relations with Libya, a human rights activist said on Thursday.

Boubakar ould Messoud of the anti-slavery SOS Esclaves group told Reuters that Messoud ould Boulkheir, whose party won the first and only opposition seat in October's parliamentary elections, and the three others had been arrested on Wednesday.

The others were Abdallahi el Atigh ould Yahi, spokesman for a group opposing normalisation with Israel, El Khory ould Hmeity, former general-secretary of the Mauritanian workers union, and Hamoud ould Abdi, a member of the national committee of the ruling Democratic and Social Republican Party.
Mauritania's relations with Libya, shunned by the West on suspicion of terrorism links, are traditionally strained, with Nouakchott accusing Tripoli of trying to destabilise it.
But Nouakchott more commonly cracks down on individuals for ties with Iraq, a country with which Mauritania traditionally enjoyed close ties until after the 1991 Gulf war over Kuwait.
Since then, Mauritania, which found itself shunned by oil-rich friends in the Gulf, has distanced itself from Baghdad and in November 1995 it even recognised Israel.
President Maaouya Ould Sid'Ahmed Taya and his ruling party won a landslide victory in October's parliamentary election.

Action for Change is a new party championing the rights of Mauritania's blacks and ex-slaves. Moors of Arab stock traditionally dominate the government of the former French colony, which straddles black and Arab Africa.
